body: SVB Financial peaked at ~$760 in Nov 2021 and failed on 10 Mar 2023 after customers tried to pull $42 bn on 9 Mar alone. Deposits had tripled 2019-21 with the VC boom (~$60 bn to ~$190 bn); SVB invested them in long-duration Treasuries/MBS, much of it classified held-to-maturity. At end-2022 unrealised HTM losses were ~$15 bn versus ~$16 bn of equity -- disclosed in the 10-K. ~90%+ of deposits were uninsured (NBER: 92.5%), concentrated in a networked VC/startup client base that was burning cash. 8 Mar: SVB announced a $1.8 bn loss on selling AFS securities and a $2.25 bn capital raise -> run. Visible flags: (1) HTM unrealised loss ~ equity (fair-value equity ~zero); (2) deposit base shrinking through 2022 as startups burned cash; (3) uninsured, concentrated deposits; (4) securities >50% of assets; no hedging of rate risk after removing swaps; (5) no chief risk officer for much of 2022; (6) CEO sold shares two weeks before failure under a pre-set plan. Lesson: for banks, mark the securities book to market and compare with equity; deposit concentration and uninsured share determine run speed. Social-media-era runs are hours, not weeks.

data.early_signals: HTM loss ~ equity; deposit outflow 2022; 90%+ uninsured; no CRO
data.lesson: Fair-value equity and deposit concentration decide bank survival
data.spotted_by: some short sellers and analysts reading the 10-K HTM footnote

title: Silicon Valley Bank (Mar 2023): duration + concentrated deposits

body: Split-adjusted ₹7.64 (Feb 2009) → ₹2,898 (Oct 2021) ≈379x; P/E ~8.5 → 93 (11x) × implied EPS ~35x. The decisive leg: ₹236 (Jun 2018) → ₹2,898 (Oct 2021) = 12x in 3.4 years, with consolidated TTM EPS ~20x (₹3.6 → ₹71.8) while P/E fell from ~69 to ~40, so it was earnings-driven. Early signal visible in filings: subsidiary Deepak Phenolics' ₹1,400 cr debt-funded Dahej phenol-acetone plant (≈200k t phenol) started commercial production on 1 Nov 2018, ran at >80% utilisation and was EBITDA/PBT positive in its first quarter; by the Dec 2020 quarter it was ~60% of revenue. This is a new segment that soon dwarfed the parent (hidden-segment pattern), an import-substitution story, plus favourable phenol spreads. Consolidated OPM 12% (FY18) → 24–29% (FY21–22). Ended: spreads normalised from 2022; consolidated EPS ~₹78 (FY22) → ~₹40 (FY26) before a Q1 FY27 rebound; the stock fell −57% (Aug 2024–Mar 2026) and is ₹1,552 (−50% from ATH ₹3,096). Lesson: capex commissioning into a spread upcycle creates explosive EPS. Price spread-driven earnings at cyclical multiples, not 90x.

data.early_signals: phenol plant COD 1 Nov 2018, >80% utilisation, EBITDA+ in first quarter
